items.text: Anton started out cutting his friends' hair. A friend's haircut is never really about the hair — he already knew what to cut. It was about the half hour of talking, every time a continuation, not awkward small talk about nothing.
Servant is *serve* and *ant* together: to serve, and Anton. The name holds both at once — the work itself, and the person doing it.
More clients came, the approach stayed the same. At most barbershops you start over every time — explain the fade you want, keep up the small talk. Here they already know you, and they know your cut.
"Where were we?" — the line Anton opens with when someone he knows sits down again. It works two ways at once: the hair, and the last thing you talked about. That line became the whole brand.
A classic barbershop serif — the vocabulary of a real trade, not a new arrival. It doesn't read as a master showing off, but as a sign of a place that has been here long enough to know everyone.

Warm brown belongs to things that age well — leather, wood, coffee, an old photograph. A place that stays and remembers everyone should be the color of what time improves, not what came new out of a box.
The line lives wherever Anton speaks to a client — in a booking reminder, on the mirror, on the card. Not a slogan, just the way he actually talks.
Servant didn't invent a value, it kept one: cut a client the way you'd cut a friend, without starting from zero. Everything else — the mark, the color, the words — just holds that in place.
